originalTitle: What HD Holders Got Paid While The Stock Fell Behind
summary: Home Depot sent its owners a torrent of cash, yet the stock trailed the market. Here is the accounting of what that trade-off actually bought, and what it means now.
content:
Home Depot sent its owners a torrent of cash, yet the stock trailed the market. Here is the accounting of what that trade-off actually bought, and what it means now.

For an investor focused on cash returns, owning Home Depot (HD) presents a paradox. Over the last five years, the home improvement retailer has handed shareholders a huge $68 billion in cash. That figure, equal to about 19.3% of the company’s entire market value today, dwarfs the $5.8 billion returned by the median S&P 500 company. The checks were generous and consistent. And yet, the stock, trading around $354.48 as of 8/11/2026, has underperformed the S&P 500 over the last twelve months (HD -6.2% vs. the S&P 500’s +22.0%), forcing owners to weigh the value of large cash payouts against lagging share price appreciation.

Image by Steve Buissinne from Pixabay

The cash machine printed a fortune for owners.

The source of this capital is the large, steady business of selling everything from paint to power tools to both do-it-yourself homeowners and professional contractors. Of the $68 billion returned to owners over five years, $42 billion arrived as direct dividend payments. The other $26 billion was used to repurchase company stock, shrinking the share count and increasing each remaining owner’s stake in the business. That buyback program has been paused since March 2024 as Home Depot works down debt from the SRS and GMS acquisitions: nearly all of the $26 billion came from FY2021–FY2023.

The stock itself delivered a different story.

Here is the paradox. While the cash payouts were exceptional, the total return for holding the stock was not. Over the same five-year period, Home Depot stock delivered a total return of +21%, dividends included. An investor holding a simple S&P 500 index fund would have seen a return of +86%. The cash returned to owners is cash that was not reinvested for growth, and the market seems to have priced the company for exactly that.

The business reason for this caution is clear in management’s own commentary: “larger discretionary projects remain under pressure” amid “greater consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure.” This is the honest catch. The torrent of cash might not be a sign of pure discipline, but of a business facing a slowdown in big-ticket spending, with fewer high-growth projects to fund. For investors who prefer the sector’s potential without concentrating on a single name, a consumer discretionary ETF like XLY offers broader exposure.

The Pro customer now carries the weight of the payout.

For the dividend checks to keep clearing, the core business must hold its ground against a difficult housing backdrop. Management’s strategy is to lean heavily into its professional customers. The company notes that its Pro segment “posted positive comps and outperformed DIY” in the most recent quarter, a sign that its investments in services and its acquisition of distributor SRS are resonating with contractors.

This is the engine the company is counting on to power through the consumer slowdown. Management is holding firm, reaffirming its full-year guidance for comparable sales growth in a range of 0.0% to 2.0%. The single thing to watch is whether its Pro customer can deliver the sales needed to hit that target.

One Generous Company Is Income. Thirty Is A Plan.

A record like this shows what disciplined capital return looks like. It is still one company’s discipline, one board’s choice, and one industry’s cash cycle, and any of the three can change.

chineseTitle: 当股票下跌时，HD 持有者得到了什么报酬
chineseSummary: 家得宝向其所有者发送了大量现金，但其股价却落后于大盘。以下是对这种权衡实际购买的东西的核算，以及它现在意味着什么。
chineseContent:
家得宝向其所有者发送了大量现金，但其股价却落后于大盘。以下是对这种权衡实际购买的东西的核算，以及它现在意味着什么。

对于注重现金回报的投资者来说，拥有家得宝（HD）是一个悖论。过去五年里，这家家居装修零售商已向股东交付了 680 亿美元的巨额现金。这一数字约占该公司目前总市值的 19.3%，使标准普尔 500 指数公司中位数的 58 亿美元回报相形见绌。这些支票是慷慨且一致的。然而，截至 2026 年 8 月 11 日，该股的交易价格约为 354.48 美元，在过去 12 个月中的表现落后于标准普尔 500 指数（HD -6.2%，而标准普尔 500 指数为 +22.0%），迫使所有者权衡大额现金支付的价值与滞后的股价升值。

该图片由Steve Buissinne在Pixabay上发布

自动提款机为业主印出了一大笔财富。

这种资本的来源是向自己动手的房主和专业承包商销售从油漆到电动工具等各种商品的庞大而稳定的业务。五年内返还给股东的 680 亿美元中，有 420 亿美元作为直接股息支付。另外 260 亿美元用于回购公司股票，减少股票数量并增加每个剩余所有者在企业中的股份。自 2024 年 3 月以来，该回购计划已暂停，因为家得宝正在减少 SRS 和 GMS 收购带来的债务：几乎所有 260 亿美元都来自 2021 财年至 2023 财年。

该股票本身却讲述了一个不同的故事。

这就是悖论。虽然现金支出非常可观，但持有股票的总回报却并非如此。在同一五年期间，家得宝股票的总回报率为 +21%（包括股息）。持有简单标普 500 指数基金的投资者将获得 +86% 的回报。返还给所有者的现金是没有再投资以实现增长的现金，而市场似乎已经为该公司定价了这一点。

这种谨慎的商业原因在管理层自己的评论中很清楚：在“消费者不确定性和住房负担能力压力更大”的情况下，“较大的可自由支配项目仍然面临压力”。这是诚实的收获。大量现金可能并不是纯粹纪律的标志，而是企业面临大额支出放缓、可供资助的高增长项目减少的迹象。对于喜欢该行业潜力而不专注于单一名称的投资者来说，像 XLY 这样的非必需消费品 ETF 可以提供更广泛的投资机会。

Pro 客户现在承担支付的重量。

为了使股息支票继续兑现，核心业务必须在困难的房地产背景下坚守阵地。管理层的策略是大力依赖专业客户。该公司指出，其专业部门在最近一个季度“取得了积极的业绩，并且表现优于 DIY”，这表明其在服务方面的投资以及对分销商 SRS 的收购正在引起承包商的共鸣。

这是该公司赖以度过消费放缓的引擎。管理层态度坚定，重申全年可比销售额增长指引在 0.0% 至 2.0% 范围内。需要关注的唯一一件事是其专业客户是否能够提供实现该目标所需的销售额。

想知道哪些公司向其所有者开出最大的支票吗？我们的回购和股息排名按现金返还总额对我们跟踪的每个名字进行排序。

一家慷慨的公司就是收入。三十是一个计划。

这样的记录显示了严格的资本回报是什么样子的。这仍然是一家公司的纪律、一个董事会的选择和一个行业的现金周期，这三者中的任何一个都可能改变。

Trefis 高质量 (HQ) 投资组合汇集了大约 30 家企业，这些企业具有为持久支出提供资金的确切特征：持续的现金生成、强劲的利润、健全的资产负债表，并按规则重新平衡它们。它有着超越三大主要指数（标准普尔 500 指数、标准普尔中型股指数和罗素 2000 指数）的基准的记录。将其应用到整个投资组合中。
